body.en: In gymnosperms the ovules are not enclosed by an ovary wall, so the seeds are naked. They are medium to tall trees and shrubs; the giant redwood Sequoia is one of the tallest trees. Roots are tap roots; Cycas has coralloid roots associated with nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria and Pinus roots have fungal mycorrhiza. The needle-like leaves of conifers, with a thick cuticle and sunken stomata, reduce water loss.
body.kn: ಅನಾವೃತಬೀಜಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಅಂಡಕಗಳು ಅಂಡಾಶಯದ ಗೋಡೆಯಿಂದ ಮುಚ್ಚಿಲ್ಲ. ಸಿಕೋಯಾ ಅತಿ ಎತ್ತರದ ಮರಗಳಲ್ಲೊಂದು. ಸೈಕಸ್‌ನ ಹವಳ ಬೇರುಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸಾರಜನಕ ಸ್ಥಿರೀಕರಿಸುವ ಸಯನೋಬ್ಯಾಕ್ಟೀರಿಯಾ ಇವೆ.

say.en: In gymnosperms the ovules sit openly on the scale, not inside an ovary: naked seeds.
Cycas has coralloid roots with cyanobacteria, Pinus has mycorrhiza, and needles save water.
Pinus bears both kinds of cones on one tree; Cycas on separate trees.
From pollen to seed: wind carries pollen, a pollen tube carries male gametes to the archegonium.
The ovule becomes a seed that stays uncovered.

body.en: Gymnosperms are heterosporous. Microsporophylls form male cones and megasporophylls with ovules form female cones. In Pinus both cones are on the same tree, while in Cycas male and female cones are on different trees. Pollen grains are carried by air currents to the ovules, a pollen tube carries the male gametes to the archegonia, and the zygote becomes an embryo. The ovules become seeds, which stay uncovered.
body.kn: ಪುರುಷ ಶಂಕು ಮತ್ತು ಸ್ತ್ರೀ ಶಂಕು ಇರುತ್ತವೆ. ಪೈನಸ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಎರಡೂ ಒಂದೇ ಮರದಲ್ಲಿ; ಸೈಕಸ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ಮರಗಳಲ್ಲಿ. ಪರಾಗ ಗಾಳಿಯಿಂದ ಅಂಡಕಗಳಿಗೆ ತಲುಪುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: A student finds a palm-like plant with pinnate leaves and only male cones on it, and coralloid roots near the soil surface. Identify it and explain the roots.

steps.en: Palm-like unbranched stem with pinnate leaves suggests Cycas.
Cycas is dioecious, so one plant bears only male cones.
Its coralloid roots hold nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria.

answer.en: Cycas; coralloid roots contain nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria
